notes.text: One more row for the reaction table, from #165: on each cycle read hkb stats --json by_model / by_shape (#155). If a shape's completion rate on the first rung falls under the board's threshold, propose the change to the human — raise kb.model on that shape's open cards, or reorder the profile's model_ladder — and never edit board.json yourself: the seat boundary in step 4 applies to model choice too. The cheap default is what the ladder in #165 does automatically (attempt 2 climbs a rung); the operator's job is to notice when a shape should not start on rung 1 at all.

One line for the operate section, learned the hard way today: **priority is a number where higher wins** (`priorityOf` in src/model.js sorts descending, then oldest issue first). Nothing in README or protocol.md says which direction it goes, and the examples use 2 and 3 without comment — the operator session filed a p2 bug believing it was urgent and watched three p4 cards go first. Say it in the skill, and add it to `hkb create --help`/README where `--priority` is introduced.

Full review of PR #167 for the continuation attempt (the attempt row keeps only 400 characters):

The deliverable matches the card in structure, is test-guarded (every EVENT_KINDS/STATUSES/OUTCOMES/BLOCK_KINDS token has a row), ships and installs correctly (`hkb init` writes operate.md in all three install shapes; 751 tests, smoke green), and tells an operator session nothing dangerous. Four text corrections before it merges — the first two would mislead a cold agent following the procedure:

1. **skills/kanban/SKILL.md ~296 and docs/wiki/features/operator-seat.md "Known gaps"**: the spend row tells the operator to read `spend.usage.by_model`. That key does not exist — `zeroUsage()` (src/stats.js ~93) has only the five token counters and live `hkb stats --json` has no `by_model` (nor `by_shape`); `attempts.by_outcome` and `spend.by_profile` are real. Drop it or future-tense it until #155 lands.
2. **SKILL.md ~305-306**: "`hkb create` for a card … filed in *triage* … not started" — `hkb create` defaults to `triage: false` (src/cli.js ~280), so a card with no blockers lands `ready` and the next tick starts it, exactly what the row forbids. Say `hkb create --triage`.
3. **Priority direction** (the comment of 00:32:58): add one line — priority is a number, **higher wins** (`priorityOf`/`sortForDispatch`, src/model.js ~353-358) — to the operate section, to `hkb create` usage (src/cli.js ~177), and to README/protocol.md where `--priority` is introduced.
4. **docs/wiki/features/web-board.md** went stale on this branch (comment-only src/init.js edit): no-op re-stamp, as hook-install-shapes.md got.

Nits, take what is cheap: ~242 "which `hkb doctor` also prints in a line" — checkMergePolicy returns null unless mode is auto, so a manual board prints nothing; ~230 "`hkb unblock` is the only thing that clears it" → "the only *operator* verb"; README ~199 "never clears kb:needs-human" contradicts the skill's own unblock-after-answering exception (the skill is right); ~311 bans "`hkb dispatch` in any form" while the manage-the-board section recommends `--dry-run` as a read-only look; the table quotes the human formatter but step 2 runs `--json` — name the JSON fields (`kind`, `to`, `outcome`, `attempt`); commands/operate.md accepts `$1` as a board slug but the section never says how it is passed (`--board <slug>` / KB_BOARD).

results.summary: The operator's seat now has a brief: `## /kanban:operate` in skills/kanban/SKILL.md, with commands/operate.md delegating to it exactly as specify.md and decompose.md do, so the procedure lives in one place and a harness with no slash commands asks the skill for the section by name. Five steps: bring the board up (hkb up --serve / --status, hkb doctor once, act on every ✗, and never hkb dispatch --loop in the foreground); watch with `hkb watch --json --interval 60` as the session's monitor (Claude Code: the Monitor tool over that command) with the three anti-habits named — no sleep-and-list, no tailing dispatch.log for state the board already has (that log answers spawn_failed and nothing else), no grepping transcripts for progress; a reaction table with a row per event kind and then per status, per outcome and per block kind, plus the dispatcher-exited-4 and the once-a-cycle `hkb stats --json` rows; the seat boundary as an explicit yours/never-yours list; and a digest per cycle. The table is a projection of the code's own vocabulary (EVENT_KINDS in src/watch.js; STATUSES/OUTCOMES/BLOCK_KINDS in src/model.js) and a new test asserts every token in all four lists has a row, so an outcome added without an operator answer fails npm test; a second new test pins the commands the procedure must name and the boundary it must state. Four rows carry lifecycle behaviour a session gets wrong otherwise: comment *then* unblock (unblock carries no answer and clears kb:needs-human, which is also why the needs-human row and the never-yours list both say 'except an answer you have just written onto the card'); dependency and transient blocks set no label while the rest do, and a third block on the same reason lands in triage; `manual` is a real merge answer; request-changes is a relaunch on the same PR. hkb init needed no code change — commandFiles() reads the directory — so only the fixed lists in test/init.test.js, test/skill.test.js and scripts/smoke-pack.mjs name the new file; src/init.js and src/doctor.js gained comment-only updates saying the set is whatever commands/ holds. Skill version 0.5.4 -> 0.6.0 (test/track.test.js pins it, deliberately, so a stale installed copy is reported stale). README's operator bullet links the command and a new subsection summarises it; docs/harnesses.md and .claude-plugin/plugin.json count three commands. Wiki: new page features/operator-seat (why the boundary must be text — every guard hkb has tests KB_TASK and an operator session has none), a targeted unstamped fix to features/planning-commands which claimed commands/ holds exactly two files, and a true no-op re-stamp of features/hook-install-shapes, the one page this branch made stale. NOTE FOR THE NEXT WORKER / THE OPERATOR: the card's second Done-when — a fresh session running the procedure end to end and handling a real review and a real needs_input — is not a worker's to do (the guard refuses `hkb up` in both layers, and driving another card's review or unblock is work belonging to other cards; also the board has no review or blocked card right now). That run is the human's, once, with /kanban:operate.

results.summary:
Continued PR #167 with the four corrections the review asked for, plus every nit, plus origin/main (#144) merged in.

(1) The spend row no longer names `spend.usage.by_model`: it does not exist. Verified against this board's live `hkb stats --json` — `spend.usage` is `{turns, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens}` (`zeroUsage()`, src/stats.js:93) and nothing more, while `attempts.by_outcome` and `spend.by_profile` are both real. The section and the wiki page's Known gaps now say a turn count and four token counters for the whole window, and say plainly that a per-model claim is one this output cannot support. (The reviewer's own 'five token counters' was one word off — four of the five keys are token counters.)

(2) `hkb create` defaults to `triage: false`, so the 'file it in triage, not started' row was telling an operator to do the thing it forbids. The row now says `--triage`, and says what happens without it: a card with no blockers lands *ready* and the next tick launches a worker on a sentence written as a note.

(3) Priority is a number and higher wins (`priorityOf`/`sortForDispatch`, src/model.js). Said once in the operate section (as a reason to leave `--priority` off — the queue's order is the human's), once in `hkb create`'s usage block (src/cli.js), once under README's first `create` example with the tie-break, and on protocol.md's machine-fields row.

(4) features/web-board.md re-stamped. It also drifted on two `src/init.js` line anchors, which are corrected.

Nits, all taken: `hkb doctor` says nothing about a `manual` board (checkMergePolicy returns null unless mode is auto), so the review row no longer implies doctor will tell you the policy — silence there is not an answer, `.kanban/board.json` is; `hkb unblock` is the only *operator* verb that clears `kb:needs-human`; the ban is now on a `hkb dispatch` that runs a tick (`--loop`, `--max`, bare) with `--dry-run` named as the read it is, in both the step-1 paragraph and the step-4 list, so the section no longer contradicts the manage-the-board section; step 3 opens by naming the `--json` fields (`number`, `kind`, `at`, `from`/`to`, `attempt`, `outcome`, `summary`, `actor`, `text`, and `tags` as what `--kinds` matches) and says the middle column is the human formatter's rendering of the same event; step 1 says how a board slug reaches the commands (`--board <slug>` or `KB_BOARD`), which is what `commands/operate.md`'s `$1` becomes. README's seat summary no longer flatly says 'never clears kb:needs-human' — it contradicted the skill's own comment-then-unblock exception — and gained 'never re-prioritises someone else's queue'.

The merge: origin/main moved (#144, worker hooks on the launch line). Conflicts in docs/harnesses.md, docs/wiki/{index,log}.md and two wiki pages. features/hook-install-shapes.md and features/web-board.md took main's version whole — #144 rewrote the first and re-anchored the second against line numbers this branch never saw — and both were then re-stamped as true no-ops for this branch's own comment-only src/init.js / src/doctor.js / smoke-pack edits, with web-board's two init.js anchors shifted by the eight lines the comment block adds. harnesses.md kept main's 'hooks ride the launch' sentence with this branch's `/kanban:operate` in the command list. log.md kept both sides and gained a line recording the resolution. index.md was regenerated. features/operator-seat.md's DENY_PATTERNS citation moved with #144's insertions (:681-689 to :724-732); every other anchor on it was re-read and had not moved.

The six pages still stale were stale at origin/main for drift this task did not verify — planning-commands.md included, as attempt 1 logged.
